item.title: 3 Falcons defenders hit with 4 fines from Week 10 loss to Chiefs
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images The Falcons racked up nine penalties in last week’s lackluster loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, but they were all procedural — there weren’t any flags for actions that typically lead to fines. But that didn’t stop the NFL from issuing four fines total to three different defensive players stemming from last Sunday’s action. Defensive lineman Brandon Dorlus was the lucky guy who got hit with two fines, each for $7,114. One was for unsportsmanlike conduct/taunting, and one was for a late hit on a quarterback. DeMarcco Hellams, who slid into the starting spot opened up by the Falcons’ decision to trade Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars before the NFL’s deadline, owes the NFL $6,509 for unnecessary roughness/a hit on a defenseless player, and linebacker Harold Perkins was also fined $5,203 for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet. The NFL splits the fine money it collects from players between the NFL Foundation to support the health, safety and wellness of athletes at all levels of football and the Professional Athletes Foundation to support NFL Legends in need. item.title: Australia hold on for narrow win against Wales
item.description: Australia secured a record win against Wales on their previous visit to Cardiff in 2024 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Nations Championship Wales (7) 26 Tries: Lake 2, Murray, Elias Cons: Costelow 3 Australia (12) 29 Tries: Tupou, Paenga-Amosa, Jorgensen, Ikitau Cons: Lonergan 2, Gordon Pens: Gordon Wales could not emulate their famous victory against New Zealand as Australia claimed the Nations Championship spoils in Cardiff. The Wallabies ended a four-match losing run thanks to tries from hooker Brandon Paenga-Amosa, prop Taniela Tupou, wing Max Jorgensen and centre Len Ikitau, while fly-half Carter Gordon kicked a late penalty. Wales captain Dewi Lake scored two tries, while full-back Blair Murray also crossed following a superb assist by wing Louis Rees-Zammit. Replacement hooker Ryan Elias grabbed a late try but Australia held on for victory as Wales paid the price for not capitalising on attacking chances. Wales finished fifth in the northern hemisphere section and will play Japan at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham on Saturday (13:10 GMT). Australia finished third in the southern hemisphere table and play Ireland on Friday (20:10 GMT). Fans flock back to the Principality Stadium After all the hysteria and celebrations to mark a first victory against the All Blacks in 73 years, the attention turned towards whether Wales could back it up against Australia. There was a vibrancy on the streets of Cardiff before the game not seen for a while, which reflected in the crowd. After crowds of 52,425 against Japan and 55,152 against New Zealand, the 66,307 attendance against Australia was the highest of the autumn. The All Blacks win proved instrumental in a surge of tickets sold for a 20:10 GMT kick-off, the latest for a Wales rugby home game at the Principality Stadium. Head coach Steve Tandy made four changes to revert to the side that beat Japan with flanker James Botham the most notable absentee following his player-of-the-match against New Zealand. Botham was expecting the birth of his first child this week but Tandy stated his omission was for rugby reasons with Cardiff colleague Alex Mann replacing him. Fit-again number eight Aaron Wainwright replaced Taine Basham, while lock Ben Carter and wing Josh Adams returned for Adam Beard and Gabriel Hamer-Webb. Australia had freshened things up with five forward changes as flanker Carlo Tizzano, lock Tom Hooper and the front-row trio of Isaac Kailea, Paenga-Amosa and Tupou came in. Australia open scoring after Llewellyn yellow card Wales lost centre Max Llewellyn inside two minutes to a yellow card for a high tackle on Wallabies full-back Tom Wright. Wallabies had plenty of early possession against 14 players but the home defence comfortably dealt with the attack. item.description: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. Getty The Philadelphia Eagles grabbed a wide receiver in the 1st round of the 2026 NFL Draft, landing USC’s Makai Lemon at No. 23 overall. That doesn’t mean he has to be their future at the position. That player will be in the 2027 NFL Draft: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. He’s on track to become the first wide receiver taken with the No. 1 overall pick since the New York Jets selected USC’s Keyshawn Johnson with the top pick in the 1996 NFL Draft. Bleacher Report’s Brent Sobleski put the Eagles at the top of his list of teams that should do whatever it takes to trade up for Smith — a deal that could easily package 1st-round picks with Lemon to make it happen. The Eagles are 2-7 and have lost 7 straight games. Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith is on par with all four as a prospect and possibly even better. NFL teams should be falling over themselves to try to acquire his services … Smith can completely change the complexion of the Eagles’ roster, especially on offense. What the team lost when it traded AJ Brown can be reinserted with a younger, more explosive version. Thus, a trio of Jeremiah Smith, DeVonta Smith and Lemon will be extremely difficult to defend, with each placed in specific roles to maximize their skill sets.” “This is a once-in-a-lifetime WR prospect right here,” Touchdown Tube wrote on its official Instagram account. item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 13: Sidney Crosby #87 of the Pittsburgh Penguins looks on against the Chicago Blackhawks during the first period at United Center on October 13, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty It had been an open secret. But now it’s official. It’s coming down to the Montreal Canadiens and Colorado Avalanche in the Sidney Crosby sweepstakes. The door is now officially open in Pittsburgh. Kyle Dubas sent a very clear message Wednesday: the Penguins are ready to make moves. With a 7-11-2 record and the team sitting near the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings, the general manager has announced a fire sale. He wants trades focused on the future, bringing in young players who can contribute to the next version of the Penguins. And in the middle of all this, there’s obviously Sidney Crosby. The captain is set to become an unrestricted free agent on July 1. If Pittsburgh decides to move him before then, Crosby himself would have to agree to a trade to a contender. Dubas acknowledged that he had spoken with his veteran players about the organization’s situation and what could happen over the coming weeks. He also emphasized his tremendous respect for Crosby and said he would respect whatever decision the captain makes. In a nutshell, Pittsburgh will trade him to whichever team he wants. In an article published in the Toronto Sun, Bruce Garrioch identified the two potential destinations that could battle for the legendary forward: Colorado and Montreal. Sidney Crosby to Avalanche? Colorado Faces Major Trade Hurdle On the Avalanche’s side, Nathan MacKinnon is Crosby’s best friend. The idea of bringing the two superstars together in the same uniform would obviously be incredibly appealing. MacKinnon would certainly love to have his close friend alongside him as they try to win another Stanley Cup. But Colorado has a major problem: its available assets. item.title: Four downs from DeWitt football's state semifinal loss to Zeeland West
item.description: CALEDONIA — Here is reaction from the DeWitt football team falling in a Division 3 state semifinal to Zeeland West 42-26 in a matchup of the last two state champions in D3. Player of the game Niko Mongkhoun, Zeeland West: The senior the tone for the Dux with an 80-yard touchdown run on the opening play of the game. Zeeland West never looked back from there and never trailed while advancing to the state final. Moungkhoun ran for 185 yards on 11 carries and recovered a fumble. Key moment DeWitt trailed 22-13 at half and was set to receive the kick to open the second half. Zeeland West recovered a squib kick to open the third quarter. Less than two minutes later the Dux had capped the drive with a touchdown and added a 2-point conversion to take a 30-13 lead. What it means DeWitt closes its season with an 10-3 record and reached the state semifinals for a third straight year. This is the second time in three seasons the Panthers have had their season end with a loss to Zeeland West in the state semifinal. DeWitt dropped to 0-3 against the Dux in the postseason. Zeeland West reaches the Division 3 state final for the second time in three years with the win and will face Harper Woods at Ford Field on Saturday, Nov. 28. Quotable "Momentum swings are big in any game but especially games of this magnitude. That (squib kick) wasn't a great start for us by any means (in the second half) but we made a lot of mistakes today and part of it is because of them and part of it is us not being as disciplined as we needed to be against a team like that on both sides of the ball and with special teams. If you're going to beat a team that doesn't make many mistakes you can't make them yourselves and we made some today for sure." DeWitt coach Rob Zimmerman Contact Brian Calloway at bcalloway@lsj.com. item.title: Chiefs Fans Slam $3 Billion Stadium Design as Clark Hunt Considers Controversial New Fee
item.description: Chiefs Fans Slam New Stadium Getty Kansas City Chiefs fans aren’t happy with the team’s plans for a new $3 billion stadium in Kansas. Many have criticized the dome design, while others are concerned they could soon have to pay more for season tickets. The Chiefs plan to leave Arrowhead Stadium and move into the new 70,000-seat venue in 2031. However, after seeing images of the proposed stadium, some furious fans questioned why the team is replacing Arrowhead’s open-air setting with a dome. Adding to their frustration, Chiefs chairman Clark Hunt confirmed the team is considering personal seat licenses (PSLs), which would require season ticket holders to pay an additional fee just to purchase their seats. Chiefs Fans Criticize New Stadium Design and Proposed Dome View this post on Instagram The planned stadium has already drawn criticism from fans who believe the design looks too similar to other modern NFL venues. Much of the frustration centers on the decision to build a dome rather than another outdoor stadium. “Sweet… looks like every other stadium built in the last ten years. I’m sure a sellout stadium will be so much better than Arrowhead,” one fan wrote on social media. Another supporter commented, “Not a single soul likes this boring, recycled dome stadium.” Others questioned whether the new venue would offer the same experience as Arrowhead, which has been the Chiefs’ home since 1972. “We do not care. Chiefs fans do not want a dome!” one X user posted. Another added, “Just like every other ugly domed stadium. No one is coming to ‘experience’ this as they do at Arrowhead. Generic trash with zero tradition or history.” Some fans also expressed frustration about not having a say in the stadium plans. “Literally nobody asked for this. The people who bought tickets for 50 years and paid for this stadium had no say in this. 90% of us hate it,” one supporter wrote. The Chiefs have not announced changes to the proposed design in response to the criticism. item.title: Wake Forest Takes Apart Georgia Tech, 50-29
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor It wasn’t pretty or artistic. While it was a blowout, it certainly was not the same type of route Wake Forest has been delivering of late; it was good enough to get the job done. Wake Forest takes apart Georgia Tech, 50-29, and gets one game closer to a spot in the ACC championship game. Wake Forest Takes Apart Georgia Tech The weather was dark, gloomy, and sometimes wet during the game. The mood on the field matched. The game was chippy from the outset. Before the game, Wake players were headed to gather in their end zone. It just so happened to be at the same time Georgia Tech was coming out of its tunnel. Words were exchanged, but nothing else. The Usual Early Start And then Wake scored early and often, and some of the aesthetic beauty of the game went by the wayside. item.description: France have won back-to-back Six Nations titles [Getty Images] Nations Championship France (14) 45 Tries: Guillard, Mauvaka, Gourgues 2, Gailleton, Duguid, Bielle-Biarrey Cons: Gourgues 5 Argentina (10) 17 Tries: Piccardo, Matera Cons: Albornoz 2 Pen: Albornoz France dispatched Argentina in Paris to book their spot against South Africa in the Nations Championship final at Allianz Stadium next Sunday. Knowing pre-game a bonus-point victory at Stade de France would be enough to edge England out of the top spot in the northern hemisphere standings, Les Bleus had to work hard to secure the points required. Lock Mickael Guillard powered over for the opening score, but Justo Piccardo responded for the visitors before Tomas Albornoz nudged them ahead with a penalty. Argentina have not been at their best this November, suffering a heavy defeat by Ireland before narrowly beating Italy. However, as is often the case with the Pumas, the longer they spend together, the more they tend to improve as a campaign progresses. Felipe Contepomi's side brought the first-half physicality needed to trouble France, who turned to their maul late in the first half to score through Peato Mauvaka and reclaim the lead. Fly-half Matthieu Jalibert, who missed the win over the world champions through injury, then expertly sent Kalvin Gourgues through a gap to score. The pivotal moment came when Argentina prop Mayco Vivas was shown a 20-minute red card for making direct head contact at a ruck, with France capitalising on the extra man to score their bonus-point try through Emilien Gailleton. Hooker Julian Montoya then joined Vivas in the sin-bin after receiving a yellow card and France made their numerical advantage count once again as Tyler Duguid and Gourgues crossed. Pablo Matera intercepted Louis Bielle-Biarrey's pass to improve the scoreline but Bielle-Biarrey made amends to dot down a brilliant kick into space by Antoine Dupont. It will now be rematch of last Friday's epic game in Paris, which France narrowly won 21-19 against the world champions. South Africa booked their spot in the final by picking up a losing bonus point against Ireland. Scotland will play Argentina on Sunday at Allianz Stadium in the seventh/eight-place play-off. item.title: Why the Alamodome's real NFL legacy endures in cities other than San Antonio
item.description: The Alamodome is seen with the San Antonio skyline on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, from the city's East Side neighborhood. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) Through the bus window, a young NBA player saw something that caught his attention. And as the Golden State Warriors rolled past downtown San Antonio on their way to Frost Bank Center, he asked a longtime member of the team's traveling party an obvious question. "Why is there a football stadium here?" the player wondered. That was two Fridays ago, and it was far from the first time in its 33-year history that the Alamodome's mere existence has served as a source of consternation. On that Warriors bus, for instance, not even those who'd been coming here for decades were sure they understood the building's intended purpose. Had they stayed through the weekend and secured a local newspaper, they might have learned a thing or two. Last Sunday, a front-page story by Express-News reporter Madison Iszler provided an in-depth look at the dome's uncertain future, which won't include another significant overhaul until at least 2035, when demolition might be one of the options on the table. The Alamodome never became the permanent home of an NFL franchise, despite the unrealistic dreams of the officials and voters who approved its construction. It eventually became obsolete, not only by the standards of the world's richest sports league, but also by those of the College Football Playoff and men's basketball Final Fours now spurning it to set up shop elsewhere. Let it not be said, however, that the Alamodome lacks a real NFL legacy. In its own way, it reshaped the geography of professional football. And across this country there are more than a couple of billionaires who owe the odd-looking structure on Montana Street a debt of gratitude, not to mention a chunk of their wealth. After all, nobody loved the Alamodome more than the owners who used it as a threat. Look around the NFL today. More than 12% of its franchises play in palaces funded at least in part by public money that was approved amid rumblings that San Antonio might be willing and able to steal those teams away. The Arizona Cardinals play in State Farm Stadium, which was built with the help of $455 million provided by Maricopa County voters in 2001 . The New Orleans Saints play in the Caesars Superdome, which was renovated after 2005's Hurricane Katrina with the help of a $41 million bond package . The Minnesota Vikings play in U.S. Bank Stadium, which was built with a combined $500 million in state and city funds approved by the Minnesota legislature and Minneapolis city government in 2012. And the Las Vegas Raiders play in Allegiant Stadium, built after the Nevada legislature approved a plan in 2016 to use $750 million in public money. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
